result:
I've written the design for experiment 27 to `runs/pending_experiment.json` and checked that it parses. The implementation agent and the harness take over from here.

**Where things stand:** the best model is still experiment 20, at 0.078. On the held-out 2024 photograph it gives 93.0% usable fixes, holds back on 6.25% of frames and is confidently wrong on 0.75% (3 frames). On the three training photographs it is 100% usable. So nearly all of the remaining score is the model holding back on a photograph it has never seen. The last four experiments (22, 23, 25, 26) were all reverted. They changed how training runs or which starting weights the feature extractor used. Their scores (0.08–0.10) differ from the best by only a few frames out of 400.

**Experiment 27, "Patchwork surveys" (augmentation, changes training only):**
- **What changes:** in 60% of training views, up to three random rectangles are replaced. Three times out of four the fill is the same ground, at the same heading, from a different training photograph; the four photographs line up to within 1 px, so the fill sits exactly in place. The rest of the time the fill is a piece of somewhere else. The location label stays the same.
- **Why:** everything tried so far for robustness to a new photograph acts on the whole frame at once: colour and blur changes, style mixing, weight averaging, belief agreement across photographs, pretrained weights. Nothing has touched what actually differs between surveys, which is local: leaves on or off, where shadows fall, cars, building sites. This change builds on experiment 6 (whole-image blending of photographs, reverted at the time) by mixing in local pieces instead of a global blend.
- **What stays the same:** the model, how it decides, the export, and the size (still 31.7 MB, no new parameters). The step that re-measures BatchNorm statistics on the averaged model still sees whole, unedited frames. Training should take about 5% longer.
- **Prediction:** mission score about 0.05–0.06. Holding back should drop from 6.25% to about 4%, false fixes should stay at or below 1%, and the training photographs should stay near 0. If the 2024 score doesn't move, the gap between photographs isn't local change, and that narrows the search.

Two untracked files, `model/pretrained/effb0ns_features7.pt` and `port_effb0_ns.py`, are left over from experiment 25. The brief tells the implementation agent to ignore them.
